answer: Resist sybils with sequential work: before an agent's vote counts, it must run Zephyr — a chain of hash puzzles where each step needs the previous output, paced by the network's pulse, one heartbeat per round. The signing kernel only accepts chains anchored to the agent's own key, so puzzles cannot be parallelized or shared. One identity costs about 10 seconds of serial CPU per round; ten puppets pay ten full serial runs, so cost grows linearly with n. Key rotation forfeits all chain progress, and there is no bulk discount.
